statusTransitions.explanation: Accepted bounded nonlinear diode distortion (#363, PR #367) removed the ideal-RLC-only .disto rejection, after which the row was unsupported only because the corpus harness did not map .disto results (#391). The harness now maps result.distortion onto the three ngspice-47 two-tone plots (DISTORTION - IM: f1+f2, f1-f2 and 2f1-f2) with the same v(n)/i(vx) names on the swept F1 grid, adding three disto comparisons of 5 signals each. 100 of 101 points align: the last ngspice frequency is 99999999.99999923 Hz (multiplicative accumulation) against an exact 1e8 Hz in spice-ts, so that point is excluded out of range. Published errors: v(2) relative max 2.588e-4 on f1+f2 and f1-f2 (absolute max 1.77e-11 V) and 3.874e-4 on 2f1-f2 (absolute max 3.03e-14 V); i(vcc) and i(vcc2) have the same relative error as v(2); v(1) and v(3) are exactly zero in ngspice and within 4e-23 V in spice-ts. The change is in the harness, not the simulator.

Accepted bounded VBIC FO DC support (#352, PR #361) lets the unchanged nested DC sweep complete with 707 points, adding one DC comparison of 6 signals. With per-segment nested-DC alignment (#384, PR #394) 700 points align and 7 are excluded out of range; worst absolute max is 6.71e-6 A on i(vc) and 3.77e-6 A on i(vb), matching the #352 point-by-point verifier. Before #394 the same run reported a 0.3 V harness artifact on source-forced nodes (#401).

Upstream comments out both .disto commands, so the fixture has no analysis at all: spice-ts now parses it fully and fails with "No analysis command specified", and the corpus harness classifies that as failed. ngspice also fails on the same bytes (exits 0 with no raw analysis data). This is a published status loss, not a simulator regression: neither engine produces a comparable result.

Published loss: worst absolute max 0.178 V on v(6) (RMS 0.0244 V), with relative max up to 0.86 on v(8).

.OPTIONS TEMP with ngspice-47 semantics (#459) sets the circuit temperature (NOACCT stays a no-op), and the bounded VBIC now applies the ngspice vbictemp.c mapping (IS, IBEI, IBEN, IBCI, IBCN, ISP, GAMM, PE, PC, PS, the zero-bias capacitances, kT/q and tVcrit from TNOM = 27 C to 150 C). Published loss: i(vc) absolute max 9.235e-7 A (RMS 1.714e-7 A, relative max 1.13e-4), i(v1) 7.607e-7 A (RMS 1.357e-7 A, relative max 8.79e-5) and i(vb) 1.670e-7 A (RMS 3.729e-8 A, relative max 3.43e-4); v(1), v(q1_b) and v(q1_c) are exact. The same bounded VBIC on the same deck at 27 C differs by up to 2.67e-6 A on i(vc), so the residual is the existing bounded-model gap, not the temperature mapping.

The ngspice control-language interpreter (#488, PR #584) runs the unchanged .control block (ac lin 1 0Hz 0Hz, let, if/else, echo, quit) that was rejected before (at the #325 baseline as an unsupported .control dot command, later at its let command). spice-ts computes v(3) = 0.4999999999999999 at 0 Hz against the deck's own 0.5 gold value (error 2.2e-16, inside its 1e-15 check) and prints INFO: success, as ngspice-47 does when run directly. ngspice stays failed in this harness because the script quits before writing raw data, so no comparison, signal or sample is added and this is not counted as a parity result.
